subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public prime/jitter scheduling contract for cron `every` and heartbeat, and if so should it be opt-in or default-on for existing configs?
rationale: The requested behavior changes scheduling semantics and public config/CLI/docs surfaces; source inspection shows a real missing cron `every` capability, but repository policy treats defaults and config additions as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Opt-in jitter/prime contract
options.body: Add explicit config/CLI fields for cron `every` and heartbeat resolution while preserving existing fixed interval semantics for current users.

options.title: Default-on phase spreading only
options.body: Extend deterministic phase spreading to cron `every` without prime interval changes, accepting a smaller API surface but still changing runtime timing behavior.

options.title: Keep current scheduling model
options.body: Leave heartbeat phase spreading and cron-expression staggering as the only built-in mitigations and document manual odd intervals or expression schedules for operators.

recommendation.title: Opt-in jitter/prime contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit config/CLI fields for cron `every` and heartbeat resolution while preserving existing fixed interval semantics for current users.

likelyOwner.reason: They appear in recent cron scheduling/docs history and were mentioned on the issue timeline, making them the best available owner for the cron `every` API direction.
